_readme: Handbag search spec. Copy to handbags.json, edit, and paste into the userscript's Settings box before a bag scan (it replaces the suit config there; re-paste config.json to go back). Analyse with: python analysis/analyze.py --config handbags.json --out bags data/*.json. Every list filter takes include_any (keep only items matching at least one; items where nothing was detected pass) and exclude (drop items matching any). Delete a filter or leave its lists empty to allow everything.

styles._options: shoulder, crossbody, tote, top handle, satchel, clutch, hobo, bucket, backpack, belt bag, flap, wallet on chain, baguette, camera, duffle

colors._options: black, white, ivory, cream, beige, taupe, grey, tan, camel, brown, cognac, chocolate, burgundy, bordeaux, red, pink, orange, yellow, green, olive, khaki, blue, navy, purple, silver, gold, metallic, multicolor, neutral, nude, monogram, damier, logo

materials._options: lambskin, calfskin (incl. togo/epsom/clemence/swift/box), caviar, patent, suede, leather, canvas, nylon, raffia, denim, tweed, velvet, shearling, exotic, intrecciato

hardware._options: gold, silver, palladium, ruthenium, gunmetal, brass, rose gold

size_words._note: Matched in the title only (e.g. 'Medium Classic Flap', 'Neverfull MM').

dimensions._note: Inches, from TRR's 'Estimated item measurements'. Unlike suits these are hard limits, because a bag can't be tailored. target is optional and only affects ranking.

vocab._note: Optional: override any built-in word list (styles, colors, materials, hardware, size_words, includes). Remove this block to use the defaults.

_designers_note: models are matched in the title/description and used to group comps (e.g. Lady Dior vs Saddle). Longest names match first.

scrape._note: url_filter is a regex. TRR's bag URL path wasn't checked live, so it's deliberately loose. Adjust it after looking at a real bag URL. price_to is above max_price so comps aren't truncated.
